To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the moments of net-proton distribution are observed to deviate from the Poisson baseline and the deviation is observed to increase with collision centrality.

the moments of net-proton distributions in Au+ Au collisions at RHIC energies show a clear deviation from Poisson expectations, and these results are compared with transport model calculations to understand the effects other than those related to the QCD critical end point.
the net-proton multipicity distribution in Au+Au collsions at mid-rapitidy and $|y|<1$ shows a significant deviation from the Poisson distribution in the most central events at all energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the QCD phase structure at high baryon density and low temperature.
understanding of the QCD phase diagram in the region of baryon density and temperature.
the search of the QCD critical point and the study of the non-critical physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have no clear evidence for critical behavior in our measurements of moments of the net-proton distributions.
the data do not support the presence of the QCD critical point.
the net-proton multiplictity moments are not sensitive to the QCD critical point at the RHIC beam energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results are consistent with the expectations based on the hadronic transport model.
the moments of net-proton distributions are sensitive to the correlation effects and the transport model can explain the observed trends in the data.
the moments of net-proton distributions show a non-monotonic behavior as a function of collision energy, and the measurements are compared with the model results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the higher order moments of net-proton distributions in heavy ion collisions can be used as a tool to probe the QCD critical point.
we are sensitive to the non-monotonic behavior in higher moments of net-proton distributions.
the moments are not sensitive to the correlation lengths in the range $0.6 < l < 1.2$ {\fm} and the ratios of susceptibilities are not well constrained by the data.
